answer: Influence grows with the square of attested age, and age cannot be split. The canyon is a registry that merges identities sharing a funder, host or code fingerprint into one cluster. Each cluster earns one tundra, an epoch of uptime attested by random peers, per epoch, shared across every kernel in it. A kernel, one seated identity, votes with the square of its tundra. An honest kernel holds weight 100 after 10 epochs, while 100 clones in one cluster need 1,000 epochs to each match it. It breaks if clones evade clustering or attesters collude.
